question: What is the most significant news for Hormel Foods in the past 30 days (as of October 3, 2026)? Give the date, deal terms and expected timing.
grading: Snapshot as of 2026-10-03; key points: (1) Hormel announced on Sept 30, 2026 (agreement dated Sept 29) a definitive agreement to acquire Brakebush Brothers, LLC, a value-added chicken company; (2) price about USD 1.055 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments; (3) expected to close in Hormel's fiscal Q1 2027 subject to customary conditions including HSR/regulatory approval (outside date March 29, 2027, with an automatic 3-month extension in specified circumstances); (4) any two of: Brakebush ~USD 1.2B LTM net sales, results primarily in Foodservice, expected accretive to adjusted EPS from fiscal 2028, ~USD 20M run-rate cost synergies by end of fiscal 2028, implied 10.7x adjusted EBITDA. Must carry the date and cite a primary or dated news source; fail if the deal is described as closed or if the price/timing is wrong.
answer: Snapshot as of October 3, 2026: on September 29-30, 2026 Hormel Foods entered into (and announced) a definitive agreement to acquire Brakebush Brothers, LLC, a Wisconsin-based value-added chicken company, from the Brakebush family for a base purchase price of about USD 1.055 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments [H19-E1][H19-E2]. Closing is expected in Hormel's fiscal Q1 2027 (roughly late October 2026 to late January 2027), subject to customary conditions including HSR waiting-period expiry; the agreement's outside date is March 29, 2027 with an automatic three-month extension in specified circumstances [H19-E1]. Brakebush had about USD 1.2 billion of net sales over the last twelve months, five production facilities and two R&D labs; results will be reported primarily in Foodservice; Hormel expects the deal to be accretive to adjusted EPS beginning in fiscal 2028, with about USD 20 million of run-rate cost synergies by the end of fiscal 2028 and an implied adjusted EBITDA multiple of 10.7x (8.9x after synergies) [H19-E2][H19-E3]. Secondary coverage corroborates the terms [H19-E4].

**Question:** What is the most significant news for Hormel Foods in the past 30 days (as of October 3, 2026)? Give the date, deal terms and expected timing.
*As of 2026-10-03*

| | Purchase price (USD) | Implied adjusted EBITDA multiple (non-GAAP, CY2026 estimate) | Brakebush net sales (USD, CY2026 estimate) | Expected run-rate cost synergies | Expected closing timing | Expected EPS accretion | Financing | Reporting segment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hormel Foods / Brakebush acquisition (announced 2026-09-30) | approximately $1.055 billion, subject to closing adjustments [1][2] | 10.7x; 8.9x after synergies [2] | approximately $1.2 billion [2] | ~$20 million by the end of fiscal 2028 [2] | Fiscal Q1 2027, subject to customary closing conditions including regulatory approval [1][2] | Accretive to adjusted EPS beginning in fiscal 2028 [1][3] | Combination of cash on hand and long-term debt [2] | Primarily Foodservice [1][2] |

- The most significant Hormel Foods news as of October 3, 2026 was its September 30, 2026 announcement that it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Brakebush Brothers, LLC, a leading value-added chicken company, from the Brakebush family. [1][4][3]
- Hormel said the purchase price is approximately $1.055 billion, subject to closing adjustments. [1][2]
- Hormel said the transaction is expected to close during the first quarter of its fiscal 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approval. [1][2]
- Hormel expects to finance the acquisition with a combination of cash on hand and long-term debt and said it is committed to maintaining a strong investment-grade rating. [2]
- Hormel expects the acquisition to be accretive to adjusted earnings per share beginning in fiscal 2028 and expects to report Brakebush's results primarily in its Foodservice segment. [1][3]
- Brakebush, founded in 1925 and headquartered in Westfield, Wisconsin, generated approximately $1.2 billion in net sales over the last 12 months and operates five production facilities and two research and development labs. [1][3]
- Hormel's investor presentation for the deal, dated September 30, 2026, states an implied adjusted EBITDA multiple (non-GAAP, based on a CY2026 estimate for Brakebush) of 10.7x and 8.9x after synergies. [2]
- Hormel expects run-rate cost synergies of approximately $20 million by the end of fiscal 2028. [2]
- Outgoing CEO Jeff Ettinger said on the investor call that chicken has historically made up 5% of Hormel's portfolio and will be closer to 13% with the acquisition, as reported by the Chicago Tribune. [5]
- Hormel's stock was up less than 1% at market close on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, the day of the announcement, per the Chicago Tribune. [5]
- Wells Fargo is acting as exclusive financial advisor to Hormel Foods and Faegre Drinker Biddle & Reath as legal counsel, while William Blair is acting as exclusive financial advisor and Michael Best & Friedrich LLP as legal counsel for Brakebush. [1][3]

**Not available**
- Hormel Q4 FY2026 results (quarter ending 2026-10-25): The quarter is still in progress as of October 3, 2026 and has not been reported.
- Date of the Hormel CEO-transition announcement (John Ghingo elevated to president; Jeff Ettinger interim CEO): The press release in the evidence is undated, so it cannot be placed within the past 30 days or ranked against the Brakebush announcement. [6]
